title: Runtime greedy scheduler with architecture probe experiments
creator: Sofia Ramos
description: Implement and evaluate a low-overhead greedy scheduling strategy that probes a small set of candidate kernels on first request slices to choose an optimal kernel for the remainder of a session. The approach should be architecture- and sequence-length-aware, targetting p50/p95 latency budgets for interactive flows while preserving throughput for batch/prefill. Deliverables: microbenchmark harness, runtime integration (catalog + decay-based online update), metrics/alerting, canary rollout plan.
acceptance_criteria:
1) End-to-end probe+select path in runtime that completes within configured probe latency budget (<=5ms added on p50).
2) Per-model/per-arch/per-seqlen profile stored in catalog and used for subsequent requests.
3) Observable reduction in p95 latency regression cases during decode-heavy workloads on canary cluster.
4) Fallback selector for missing profiles that keeps latency within safe SLOs.
5) Unit and e2e tests + benchmarking dashboards linked in ticket.
design_notes:
- Probes should be synthetic short tokens (e.g., 16 tokens) executed on-path in the first request window, collected with warmup disabled to reflect cold-to-warm behavior.
- Bucketing: {<=32, 33-128, 129-512, >512} tokens.
- Profile dimensions: kernel_variant, arch_family (A100/V100/RX), quantization mode, occupancy estimate, observed latency distribution.
- Selection heuristic: greedy choose-min-latency constrained by memory/kv-cache usage and probe-cost amortization over expected session length.
- Online update: exponentially weighted moving average (alpha=0.2) with decayed historical influence across 24h window.
- Safety: if probe fails or probe cost > budget, default to conservative kernel with bounded latency and higher throughput cost.
tradeoffs:
- Probing increases initial latency slightly but can reduce long-run p95; need to tune probe budget vs expected session length.
- Bucketing granularity improves accuracy but increases catalog cardinality and storage; we choose coarse buckets to limit explosion.
- Warmup-free probes are cheaper but may under-estimate real decode latency for long-running contexts; mitigate by combining with periodic background microbench when load is low.
- Aggressive selection towards fastest kernel may regress output quality in quantized kernels; add quality flag and avoid selection for high-quality sensitive models.
plan:
1) Spike (2d): implement microbenchmark harness and run across available infra (A100, T4, AMD) to produce baseline profiles.
2) Prototype (3d): wire probe invocation into runtime request path behind feature flag; store selection decisions in a local in-memory cache.
3) Integration (5d): persist profiles to Runtime Catalog, implement decay-based updater, and add metrics.
4) Canary (3d): route 5% traffic, monitor latency, token cost, error rate, and quality regressions.
5) Rollout (2d): widen to 25% if metrics stable, then full if green.
